newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish banks' net soars to PLN 2.9 bln in H1 1996.
newsitem.headline: Polish banks' net soars to PLN 2.9 bln in H1 1996.

text.p: Polish banks registered a net profit of 2.9 billion zlotys in the first half of this year, 129.6 percent more than in the same period of 1995, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
GUS said in a report that banks' gross profit in the January-June period rose to 3.9 billion from 2.1 billion last year.

It said that after the central bank pared official interest rates in January, sparking cuts in credit rates throughout the banking sector, revenue from interest fell to 8.5 billion zlotys from 10 billion in the first half of 1995.

GUS said the financial situation of banks improved in the first half of 1996 because they created less costly strategic reserves. Strategic reserves totalled some 800 million zlotys in the six-month period, down from 1.3 billion last year.
